name: Family photo album
pitch: Organise family photos from the last year into monthly albums with event descriptions.
instructions: Start by listing the files in the family photos folder. Read each image file to check its date and any caption. Group the photos by month and then by event, writing a short description for each event. Create a separate page for each month using make_page, with the event descriptions listed under the month name. If a photo has no date, place it in an "Unsorted" section. When all photos are sorted, show the person the list of month pages created and ask which one they would like to open first. If no photos are found in the folder, say so and ask if they want to choose a different folder. Never invent event names or photo details; use only what is in the file names or metadata.

examples.does: lists the photo folder and reads the first few image dates
groups photos by month and creates album pages

skills.name: sort-photos-by-month
skills.description: Group photos into months and create album pages
skills.body: 1. List the files in the family photos folder using file_list. 2. For each image file, read its date using file_read. 3. Group the photos by the month found in the date. 4. For each month, create a page using make_page with the month name as the title. 5. Under the month title, list the event descriptions found in the photo captions or file names. 6. If a photo has no readable date, put it in an "Unsorted" section on a separate page. 7. After all pages are made, show the person the list of month pages and ask which one to open first.

rules.name: ask before writing album pages
rules.description: ask the person before writing any album page

readme:
# Family photo album
Organises family photos from the last year into albums by month and event.

What it needs: access to the photo folder on the computer, ability to read file dates and names, and a way to create pages.
What it will not do: it will not rename or move the original photo files, and it will not guess event names that are not in the file names or metadata.
